decoding.temperature: provider default (temperature/top_p unsupported on reasoning models)
decoding.reasoning_mode: native (reasoning content returned in a separate field)

design.excluded: 2 empty-output cells, both self_refine (s79 seed 2, s185 seed 0); scorer seed-averages over remaining seeds per protocol. Headline control/instruction stats unaffected.

normalization.why: generation hygiene flagged 94% markdown and 100% title lines (formatting the plain-prose human baseline lacks; guard: experiments/ablation/generation_hygiene.py). Uniform R1-6 protocol: every leg is normalized before scoring.
normalization.effect: scored on normalized text; raw scoring archived beside the normalized eval on the HF dataset.

scoring.test: one paired Wilcoxon signed-rank per (mode, metric) over 200 seed-averaged headline pairs, delta = human - model

generation.driver: bench/run.py (openai_compat provider, api.x.ai/v1, max_tokens 16000, checkpoint-resumable JSONL)

duration: ~2h30m API run (8 workers), single-cell resume for 1 transient error
cost_usd: $17.50 actual from telemetry: 3,073,396 in @ $2/M + 1,892,744 out @ $6/M (grok-4.5 launch pricing)
headline_finding: First family where the dispersion gap INVERTS: under instruction, Grok 4.5 text is significantly MORE dispersed than human (B_n delta -0.025 p=0.015, Gini -0.014 p=0.012), and its segmentation entropy exceeds human in both modes (control -0.249, rb -0.74). The human-AI burstiness gap is not monotone across frontier generations.
provenance: Generated via the xAI API against pinned prompts; hygiene-gated, normalized (R1-6 uniform protocol), and scored locally against the frozen human baseline on the post-R1-5 metric; compiled eval carried into the repo as SSOT.
